rules.tag: format is exactly "vaultody vault keys v1"; anything else (another version, another case, missing, not a string, a top level that is not an object) is unknown_format. No migration from earlier layouts.
rules.layout: { format, origins: { origin: { responseSignature: null | { latchedAt, rootId: text | null }, vaults: { vaultId: pin }, audit: [ { vaultId, at, reason, removed } ] } } }; the latch's rootId is null when the signed answer that set it did not verify; pin = { vaultId, type: main|test, keys: { ECDSA: xpub|null, EDDSA: xpub|null } (at least one xpub), status: verified|unverified, firstSeenAt, verifiedAt, verification: null | { rootId, timestamp } }; verified ⇔ verifiedAt and verification set.
rules.strict: Every field is required and no other is allowed, at any level; anything that differs is malformed. A refused file is never treated as empty.
rules.origin: scheme://host[:port] (http or https), no path, no trailing slash: ^https?://[^/?#@\s]+$
rules.times: Unix seconds, a JSON integer token (no fraction, no exponent), 0 to 2^53 − 1.
rules.errors: VaultKeyStoreError with code not_json (not strict UTF-8 JSON, a byte-order mark, empty), unknown_format, malformed, insecure_permissions (POSIX mode & 022), not_regular_file (a symbolic link, a directory), too_large (over 16 MiB). Checked in that order of the file first: regular file, mode, size, then the bytes.
rules.canonical: A writer writes UTF-8 with object keys sorted at every level, a two-space indent, ": " after a key, "/" and non-ASCII characters unescaped, and a final newline: JSON.stringify(sorted, null, 2) + "\n", Python json.dumps(indent=2, sort_keys=True, ensure_ascii=False) + "\n".
rules.storeErrors: Besides the file codes above, VaultKeyStoreError has, the same in every language: unreadable (an I/O error reading), unwritable (it can't be written), locked (the lock was held for 10 s), invalid_pin (a pin or latch handed to the store that the file can't hold), store_conflict (a pin changed in the store between the client's read and its write, by another writer; nothing is returned, calling again reads afresh).
rules.files: A missing file is an empty store. Writes: directory 0700, a temporary file 0600 in it, synced, renamed over the file; a read-change-write holds <file>.lock, created exclusively (O_CREAT|O_EXCL, 0600) and removed afterwards; a lock older than 30 s is stale; a writer gives up after 10 s (locked). Readers take no lock.

caseFormat.valid: { name, text, expected: { origins } }: the text parses, and for each origin the store lists exactly its pins (sorted by vaultId) and returns its latch
caseFormat.invalid: { name, text | base64, expected: { error } }: refused with that code
caseFormat.files: { name, mode | symlinkTo | directory | absent, content: a valid case name or "invalid:<name>", posixOnly, expected: { origins } | { error } }: the file is set up so, then read through the file store
caseFormat.canonical: { name, document, text }: what every SDK writes for document, byte for byte
